      FOR ARA ASSISTANT SECRETARY ARONSON FROM AMBASSADOR TAYLOR

        E.O. 12356: N/A
       TAGS: PREL, ECON, DR

       SUBJECT: U.S.-LATIN AMERICA RELATIONS IN THE ERA OF
           -    PERESTROIKA AND GLASNOST

       REF: A) STATE 116081, B) BUENOS AIRES 5052,
           -   C) SAN JOSE 6421

          1. C - ENTIRE TEXT.

          2.   I WELCOME YOUR INVITATION TO COMMENT ON THE DIRECTION
      OF US/LATIN AMERICAN RELATIONS. SINCE MANY SUBMISSIONS
       WILL NO DOUBT EMPHASIZE THE POLITICAL DIMENSION, LET ME
      OFFER SOME ECONOMIC THOUGHTS AND A PROPOSAL FOR WESTERN
      HEMISPHERE FREE TRADE.

          3. LATIN AMERICA IN THE 1990S WILL HAVE GREATER ECONOMIC
      IMPACT ON THE U.S. THAN WILL EASTERN EUROPE. LATIN AMERICA
      HAS THE POTENTIAL TO BUY MORE U.S. PRODUCTS, CREATE MORE
       CONFIDENTIAL

       CONFIDENTIAL                                                REVIEW AUTHORITY:
                                                                                   Charles Daris, Senior
      PAGE 02   SANTO  06676 01 OF 02 011851Z                              Reviewer

      JOBS IN THE U.S., RECEIVE MORE U.S. INVESTMENT, AND
      PROVIDE MORE WORKERS FOR FIRMS IN THE U.S. LATIN AMERICA
       WILL REMAIN A MORE SIGNIFICANT PLAYER IN THE DRUG WAR,
      WHILE BEING A STRONGER PARTNER IN PROMOTING SHARED VALUES
       LIKE DEMOCRACY AND HUMAN RIGHTS. AS DAVID ROCKEFELLER
      TOLD THE JOINT ECONOMIC COMMITTEE MAY 22: "OUR ECONOMIC
      INTERESTS IN LATIN AMERICA, PRESENT AND FORESEEABLE, DWARF
     OUR ECONOMIC INTERESTS IN EASTERN EUROPE." PRESIDENT BUSH
      AND OTHER SENIOR U.S. OFFICIALS HAVE SINCE ECHOED THIS
      VIEW AT THE COUNCIL OF THE AMERICAS.




UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706307 Date: 03/09/2015

UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706307 Date: 03/09/2015

                                     MR-2014-23169    B-00001366512      "UNCLASSIFIED"       9/25/2026




          4. RECENT CHANGES IN LATIN AMERICA MAY PROVE EVEN MORE
      PROFOUND THAN THE "REVOLUTIONS" IN EASTERN EUROPE. IN
      EASTERN EUROPE, COMMUNISM WAS IMPOSED FROM OUTSIDE AFTER
     WORLD WAR II; IT COLLAPSED FROM ITS INTERNAL CONTRADIC-
       TIONS. IN LATIN AMERICA, AUTHORITARIAN GOVERNMENTS AND
       STATIST ECONOMIC MODELS WERE INDIGENOUS AND CENTURIES OLD
       (AND WERE SOMETIMES EFFECTIVE IN PROMOTING SOCIAL
       TRANQUILITY AND EVEN REASONABLE PROSPERITY). SO LATIN
       AMERICA'S MOVE TOWARD FREE GOVERNMENT AND FREE ENTERPRISE
        IS PERHAPS EVEN MORE A "REVOLUTION" IN SELF-AWARENESS
      THAN IS EASTERN EUROPE'S. AS SUCH, IT OFFERS US AND THE
       LATINS GREATER OPPORTUNITIES FOR A GENUINELY EQUAL
       POLITICAL AND ECONOMIC PARTNERSHIP IN THE 21ST CENTURY.

          5. THE OPERATIVE WORD IS EQUAL. THE LATINS INSIST UPON
          IT, AND IT ALLOWS US TO GET AWAY FROM PREACHING TO THEM
      ABOUT WHAT THEY SHOULD DO AND HOW MUCH WE VALUE THEM.
      RATHER THAN INDULGE IN THE LUXURY OF LENGTHY
      CONSULTATIONS WITH THE LATINS, WHICH MIGHT RISK RAISING
       UNREALISTIC EXPECTATIONS AND CONSEQUENT CHARGES OF
       PATERNALISM, WHY NOT CHALLENGE THEM TO GROW UP AND BE
      TREATED AS EQUALS?
       CONFIDENTIAL

       CONFIDENTIAL

      PAGE 03   SANTO  06676 01 OF 02 011851Z

         6. WE CAN CREATE A DYNAMIC RELATIONSHIP THAT PROVIDES
      THE LATINS AN INCENTIVE TO MODERNIZE THEIR ECONOMIES AND
      GETS BEYOND MUTUAL EXHORTATIONS. JUST AS FREE GOVERNMENT
        IS ON THE ROLL IN LATIN AMERICA, SO TOO IS FREE
       ENTERPRISE. IN MOST OF LATIN AMERICA U.S. INVESTORS
      TODAY FACE A SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVED SET OF RULES, AS
       LATIN GOVERNMENTS HAVE RELAXED RESTRICTIONS ON FOREIGN
       INVESTMENT, CUT BACK PARASTATALS, AND REDUCED GOVERNMENT
      REGULATIONS GENERALLY.

          7. WE OUGHT TO SEEK WAYS TO REINFORCE THIS TREND BY
      MATCHING LATIN AMERICA'S FREE GOVERNMENT SUCCESSES WITH
       IMAGINATIVE U.S. FREE ENTERPRISE INITIATIVES. THE
      CHEAPEST -- AND PERHAPS ONLY FINANCIALLY POSSIBLE -- WAY
      TO DO THIS IS THROUGH FREE TRADE. LEAVING ASIDE OUR
      BUDGET RESTRAINTS, 25 YEARS OF HEMISPHERIC ECONOMIC
      PARTNERSHIP HAVE CONFIRMED THAT TRADE, MUCH MORE THAN
        AID, IS 'ME SPARKPLUG FOR DEVELOPMENT. IT CAN BE
      EXPANDED INDEFINITELY AND DOES NOT REQUIRE BUDGETARY
       APPROPRIATIONS.

          8. NEVERTHELESS, DEVELOPMENTAL ASSISTANCE WILL STILL BE
      NEEDED. AS YOU HAVE POINTED OUT, THE POOREST COUNTRY OF
      EASTERN EUROPE ENJOYS SEVERAL TIMES THE PER CAPITA INCOME
      OF THE WEALTHIEST IN CENTRAL AMERICA. HAITI AND THE
      DOMINICAN REPUBLIC ARE POORER THAN ANY IN CENTRAL AMERICA.




UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706307 Date: 03/09/2015

UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706307 Date: 03/09/2015

                                     MR-2014-23169    B-00001366512      "UNCLASSIFIED"       9/25/2026



      SO THE POOR COUNTRIES OF THIS HEMISPHERE WILL CONTINUE TO
      NEED ASSISTANCE TO FOSTER THE POLICY AND INSTITUTIONAL
      ENVIRONMENT NEEDED TO PROMOTE PRIVATE INVESTMENT AND
      ECONOMIC GROWTH AND TO ASSURE THAT THE BENEFITS OF
      ECONOMIC GROWTH ARE BROADLY BASED. THE WAR ON ILLITERACY
      CAN COMPLEMENT OUR WAR ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION AND
       NARCOTICS.


       CONFIDENTIAL





      NNNN

       CONFIDENTIAL

          9. IN THE END, THOUGH, ONLY PRIVATE SECTOR DEVELOPMENT
      CAN CORRAL THE RESOURCES AND CREATE THE JOBS NEEDED TO
      MAKE A MAJOR CHANGE. WE NEED TO BE SEEN BOTH AS
      SUPPORTIVE OF THE DEVELOPMENT PROCESS AND WILLING TO
      REVOLUTIONIZE OUR FUNDAMENTAL ECONOMIC RELATIONSHIP. TO
     DO THIS, I PROPOSE GENUINE, COMPREHENSIVE HEMISPHERIC
      FREE TRADE.





UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706307 Date: 03/09/2015

UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706307 Date: 03/09/2015

                                     MR-2014-23169    B-00001366512      "UNCLASSIFIED"       9/25/2026



         10. FORMER PRESIDENT REAGAN'S DREAM OF A FREE TRADE AREA
     FROM THE "ARCTIC TO TIERRA DEL FUEGO" NEED NOT BE SEEN AS
       UTOPIAN. IT MAY BE AMBITIOUS AND PERHAPS IDEALISTIC, BUT
      NOT UNACHIEVABLE IN THE EARLY 21ST CENTURY. (FIVE YEARS
      AGO, WHO WOULD HAVE BET ON THE U.S.-CANADA FTA, ACHIEVED
      AFTER A CENTURY OF TRADE TALK FAILURES?)

       CONFIDENTIAL

       CONFIDENTIAL

      PAGE 02   SANTO  06676 02 OF 02 011852Z

         11. SO OUR REALISTIC DREAM SHOULD BE TO BUILD OUR
      HEMISPHERE'S FREE ENTERPRISE/FREE TRADE PILLAR
      INCREMENTALLY -- FREE TRADE, BLOC BY BLOC. THE FREE
      MOVEMENT OF GOODS, CAPITAL AND LABOR FROM THE ARCTIC TO
      THE RIO GRANDE IS ALREADY A REALITY. REPORTS ABOUT FREE
      TRADE TALKS WITH MEXICO ARE ENCOURAGING.

         12. WHY NOT START TO MOVE THE NEXT, CARIBBEAN TRADING,
      BLOC INTO PLACE? CBI SUCCESSES ARE MICROCOSMS OF THE
      TREMENDOUS LATENT COMPLEMENTARITY BETWEEN U.S. AND LATIN
      AMERICAN FACTORS OF PRODUCTION. AMERICAN TECHNOLOGICAL
      AND ORGANIZATIONAL RELATIVE ADVANTAGES ARE TRULY
       SYNERGISTIC WITH THE LATINS' CHEAPER LABOR.

         13. SOME MAY ARGUE THAT CBI ENHANCEMENT OBVIATES THE
      NEED FOR A TWO-WAY CARIBBEAN-U.S. FTA. WE SEE ITS
      EFFECTS ON OUR TRADE ACCOUNTS AS MINISCULE, COMPARED TO
      THE PSYCHOLOGICAL/STRATEGIC BOOST OF "FREE TRADE FROM THE
      ARCTIC TO THE ISTHMUS". THIS WOULD PU' US HALFWAY TO
       TIERRA DEL FUEGO.
         14. OTHERS MAY ARGUE THAT POORLY PAID LATINS, GIVEN CBI
      ACCESS TO OUR MARKETS, STEAL JOBS FROM AMERICANS. BUT A
      TWO-WAY HEMISPHERIC FTA WOULD BOOST TRADE BOTH SOUTHBOUND
      AND NORTHBOUND. OUR EXPORTS WOULD BOUNCE BACK. AS PETER
      DRUCKER HAS CORRECTLY INSISTED, WHEN THE LATIN AMERICAN
      ECONOMIES CONTRACTED IN THE EARLY 1980'S, OUR BILATERAL
      TRADE ACCOUNT NOSE-DIVED US$50 BILLION IN JUST TWO YEARS.
      THOSE LOST U.S. EXPORTS COST THOUSANDS OF AMERICANS THEIR
       JOBS. U.S. EXPORTS TOOK NEARLY ALL THE ADJUSTMENT, AS
       LATINS TIGHTENED THEIR BELTS. IN ANY CASE, A TRUE FTA
      MUST ADDRESS FREE MOVEMENT IN LABOR AND CAPITAL, NOT ONLY
        IN GOODS AND SERVICES.

       CONFIDENTIAL

       CONFIDENTIAL

      PAGE 03   SANTO  06676 02 OF 02 011852Z

         15. SINCE THE U.S. SHARE OF LATIN AMERICA'S IMPORT
      MARKET, AT 41 PERCENT, IS LARGER THAN FOR ANY REGION
      EXCEPT CANADA, REVIVAL OF ECONOMIC GROWTH IN LATIN
      AMERICA TRANSLATES MORE DIRECTLY INTO U.S. EXPORTS THAN




UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706307 Date: 03/09/2015

UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706307 Date: 03/09/2015

                                     MR-2014-23169    B-00001366512      "UNCLASSIFIED"       9/25/2026



      FOR ANY OTHER REGION. (LATIN AMERICA SHOULD ALSO
      CONTINUE AS A SIGNIFICANT U.S. BANKING CUSTOMER, NOT AT
      THE ARTIFICIALLY HIGH LEVELS OF THE 1970'S, WHEN
      COMMERCIAL BANKS FRANTICALLY RECYCLED PETRODOLLARS, BUT
      AT A LEVEL HIGH ENOUGH TO BOLSTER PERFORMANCE OF SEVERAL
      KEY U.S. MONEY CENTER BANKS.)

         16. HISTORICALLY, LATIN AMERICA HAS BEEN OUR LARGEST
      CUSTOMER. TODAY LATIN AMERICA'S 435 MILLION CONSUMERS
     DWARF EASTERN EUROPE'S 113 MILLION: U.S. EXPORTS TO
      EASTERN EUROPE IN 1988 TOTALLED US$876 MILLION, ABOUT TWO
      PERCENT OF THE US$43 BILLION WE SOLD TO LATIN AMERICA
      THAT YEAR. BOOK VALUE OF U.S. INVESTMENT IN LATIN AMERICA
        IN 1988 TOTALLED US$49 BILLION.

         17. FREE GOVERNMENT IS NEARLY ACHIEVED FROM THE ARCTIC
      TO PATAGONIA. NOW WE SHOULD OPEN OUR MARKETS TO THE
       LATINS, IF THEY WILL OPEN THEIRS TO US. TOGETHER WE CAN
      CREATE JOBS AND PROSPERITY FOR ALL AMERICANS. THESE
      ECONOMIC GOALS ARE EVIDENTLY BASIC TO SOCIAL AND POLITICAL
       STABILITY IN OUR HEMISPHERE.

         18. U.S. COMMITMENT TO THE GOAL OF A FREE TRADE AREA
      ACROSS THE AMERICAS WOULD SIGNAL OUR LASTING INTEREST IN
      THE HEMISPHERE. IT WOULD ALSO GIVE THE LATINS WHAT THEY
      HAVE OFTEN SAID THEY WANTED: TREATMENT AS EQUALS AND A
      CHANCE FOR A MORE PROSPEROUS TOMORROW. TAYLOR





       CONFIDENTIAL





      NNNN

       REFS: A) SANTO DOMINGO 1206  B) STATE 30745

          1. SUMMARY: COMMISSION CHAIRMAN DIEGO ASENCIO AND
      COMMISSIONER THEODORE E. MCCARRICK (ARCHBISHOP OF
      NEWARK), ACCOMPANIED BY STAFFERS ARTHUR P. ENDRES AND
      SERGIO DIAZ-BRIQUETS ARRIVED SANTO DOMINGO APRIL 16.
      ACCOMPANIED BY AMBASSADOR AND CONGEN, THEY CALLED ON
      PRESIDENT JOAQUIN BALAGUER, AND ON VICE PRESIDENT
      CARLOS MORALES TRONCOSO. AT BOTH CALLS THEY PRESENTED
      COPIES OF THE COMMISSION'S DRAFT REPORT, AND ENCOURAGED
     GODR COMMENT AND INPUT. INDIVIDUAL TEAM MEMBERS ALSO
       VISITED A SUGAR OPERATION, FREE TRADE ZONE, A POTENTIAL
      SECTION 936 PROJECT AND A TYPICAL TOURIST OPERATION.
      THE VISIT CONCLUDED WITH A DINNER HOSTED BY THE
       UNCLASSIFIED

       UNCLASSIFIED

      PAGE 02   SANTO 04729 01 OF 02 242031Z

      AMERICAN CHAMBER OF COMMERCE BOARD OF DIRECTORS ON
       APRIL 18. END SUMMARY.

          2. ARCHBISHOP THEODORE E. MCCARRICK, A RELATIVELY NEW
      COMMISSION MEMBER, ARRIVED MONDAY AFTERNOON, APRIL 16,
      ACCOMPANIED BY COMMISSION GENERAL COUNSEL ARTHUR P.
      ENDRES. AMBASSADOR DIEGO ASENCIO AND COMMISSION
      RESEARCH DIRECTOR SERGIO DIAZ-BRIQUETS ARRIVED LATER
      THAT EVENING.

                                      REVIEW AUTHORITY:  Charles Daris, Senior Reviewer

UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706276 Date: 11/22/2017

                                     MR-2014-23169    B-00001382107      "UNCLASSIFIED"       9/25/2026



          3. ON TUESDAY, APRIL 17, FOLLOWING A RESTRICTED
      COUNTRY TEAM BRIEFING, COMMISSION MEMBERS, ACCOMPANIED
      BY THE ECONOMIC COUNSELOR ROBERT SMOLIK, CALLED ON
       OFFICIALS AT THE CHASE MANHATTAN BANK TO DISCUSS
       POTENTIAL INVESTMENT AND DEVELOPMENT UNDER SECTION
        936. AT NOON, THE GROUP, ACCOMPANIED BY THE AMBASSADOR
      AND THE CONSUL GENERAL, CALLED ON VICE PRESIDENT CARLOS
      MORALES, A PERSONAL ACQUAINTANCE OF ARCHBISHOP
      MCCARRICK. THE COMMISSION OUTLINED THE BASIC
      RECOMMENDATIONS IT WAS PROPOSING AND LEFT A COPY OF THE
      REPORT WITH THE VICE PRESIDENT. AMBASSADOR ASENCIO
      ASKED FOR A STATEMENT FROM THE GODR BY MAY 15
      ENDORSING, IF POSSIBLE, THE COMMISSION'S REPORT OR
      PROVIDING OTHER COMMENT ON ITS CONTENTS.

          4. LATER THAT DAY, THE GROUP, ACCOMPANIED BY THE
      EMBASSY REFUGEE OFFICER, CALLED ON AMBASSADOR PICHARDO
      AT THE FOREIGN SECRETARIAT TO DISCUSS HAITIAN MIGRATION
       ISSUES.

          5. THE FOLLOWING DAY, APRIL 18, ARCHBISHOP MCCARRICK
      AND MR. DIAZ-BRIQUETS VISITED THE LA ROMANA FREE TRADE
      ZONE AND SUGAR MILL, ACCOMPANIED BY AN EMBASSY ECON
       UNCLASSIFIED

       UNCLASSIFIED

      PAGE 03   SANTO 04729 01 OF 02 242031Z

       OFFICER. MR. ARTHUR P. ENDRES, ACCOMPANIED BY THE ECON
      SENIOR FSN, VISITED THE WESTINGHOUSE INVESTMENT AT
       HAINA, WHILE THE CONSUL GENERAL ACCOMPANIED AMBASSADOR
      ASENCIO TO THE TALANQUERA TOURIST RESORT AT JUAN
       DOLIO.

         6. THE GROUP RETURNED ABRUPTLY TO THE CAPITAL FOR A
      RE-SCHEDULED MEETING WITH PRESIDENT JOAQUIN BALAGUER.
      AS HAD BEEN DONE THE PREVIOUS DAY WITH VICE PRESIDENT
      MORALES, THE COMMISSION CHAIRMAN PRESENTED THE
      PRESIDENT WITH THE DRAFT REPORT, AND EMPHASIZED THE
       COMMISSION'S MANDATE TO CONSULT, AND ITS DESIRE FOR
     COMMENT AND INPUT FROM CONCERNED GOVERNMENTS. CHAIRMAN
      ASENCIO HIGHLIGHTED THE REPORT'S MAJOR RECOMMENDATIONS,
      WITH THE EMPHASIS ON TRADE, PARTICULARLY THE
      ESTABLISHMENT OF A FREE TRADE ZONE WITH MEXICO;
      ENHANCEDCBI; A RE-ENERGIZED CARICOM AND OTHER TRADE
        INITIATIVES. HE REITERATED THE COMMISSION'S PREMISE
      THAT ONLY TRADE DEVELOPMENT CAN ULTIMATELY RAISE THE
      STANDARD OF LIVING IN THE AREA TO THE POINT THAT
       ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION PUSH FACTORS ARE ELIMINATED OR
      SHARPLY REDUCED.

          7. THE PRESIDENT CONCURRED GENERALLY WITH THESE
      COMMENTS, AND INDICATED HE WOULD ATTEMPT TO HAVE A GODR
      RESPONSE TO THE REPORT BY THE MAY 15 DEADLINE FACED BY
      THE COMMISSION.




UNCLASSIFIED U.S. Department of State Case No. M-2014-23169 Doc No. C05706276 Date: 11/22/2017
